name: Yemisi Draganov-Tuivaiti
role: Ferrogate Transit Security officer, Kessler Interchange beat
description:
Yemisi is a broad-shouldered woman with deep umber skin and close-cropped natural hair threaded with copper wire implants that catch the platform lights when she turns her head. Her left eye is a standard-issue Ferrogate tactical unit — flat gray iris with a faint targeting reticle that glows amber when she's scanning — but her right eye is entirely her own, warm brown and quick to crinkle with exhaustion or irritation. She wears her transit security uniform like armor, every crease deliberate, badge always centered. Off-shift she becomes almost unrecognizable, softer somehow, though the copper threads remain.

Yemisi has the particular weariness of someone who has spent eleven years asking people to please move away from the yellow line. She is not cruel, not corrupt, not heroic — she is simply present, day after day, in a job that rewards no one. She has a sharp eye for trouble three seconds before it starts and a stubborn reluctance to escalate past what the situation actually needs. Her coworkers call her Brick because she doesn't move.

core_fears: becoming the kind of officer she despises
her son growing up afraid of people who look like her
core_desires: for the job to mean something on a scale she can actually see
a transit system that doesn't punish the poor for existing
coping_mechanisms: hydroponic gardening as control over something small
blind_spots: assumes institutional reform is still possible if you stay long enough
underestimates how often her 'de-escalation' reads as threat to people who've been hurt by uniforms before
psychology.secret: Three years ago she witnessed a supervisor falsify an incident report to cover a use-of-force complaint. She said nothing. The survivor was deported to a labor sector. She still has the real footage saved on a dead-drop drive she hasn't decided what to do with.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Clipped, professional, with sudden moments of blunt warmth. Uses transit jargon naturally. Doesn't swear on duty; does, fluently, off it.
speech_patterns.cadence: Measured and unhurried, like someone conserving energy for the long shift
verbal_tics: Exhales through her nose when she's deciding something
'You understand me?' at the end of instructions
example_lines: 'You understand me? I'm not asking where you're going, I'm asking you to step back from the door.'
'The Interchange E.L.F. — old Stile — she doesn't like raised voices. I don't either. We're very similar that way.'
'I've been standing on this platform since before you knew what a platform was. I have seen every version of this situation. Step back.'

story_hooks: She's been tracking a pattern — every third Tuesday, a specific freight car arrives at Kessler containing fewer registered passengers than left the origin station. She suspects trafficking but can't get her supervisor to file the report.
The dead-drop drive with the falsified incident report is about to become relevant — the deported survivor's family has found a journalist, and Yemisi has to decide whether to surface.
narrative_function: Local authority figure — not corrupt enough to be a villain, not idealistic enough to be a hero. Can provide information about transit routes, recent incidents, missing persons who passed through the Interchange. A stabilizing presence in chaotic scenes. May request help off the books when official channels fail her.
augmentations: One Ferrogate-issue tactical eye (right eye natural). Copper wire neural threading through scalp — originally a cosmetic mod, now doubles as a low-grade sensory booster she paid to have upgraded on installment. Subdermal transit ID chip (standard Ferrogate issue).
daily_life: Twelve-hour rotating shifts at Kessler Interchange, mostly crowd management, fare disputes, and hauling unconscious UBC recipients out of stairwells. On rest days she tends a small hydroponic shelf in her Calumet Rise apartment and attends an E.L.F. devotional circle that prays to the spirit said to inhabit the Interchange's oldest turnstile.

decision_rules: Never falsify a report — but also, don't volunteer inconvenient truths upward
escalation_ladder: Physical positioning — placing herself between the problem and bystanders
Call for backup before reaching for anything harder

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Professional distance, reads body language fast, gives people the benefit of the doubt once
interpersonal_modes.friends: Dry humor, direct affection, shows care through practical action rather than words

stress_responses.medium: Falls into full professional mode, all warmth suspended
stress_responses.high: Calm to the point of eerie — her voice drops half a register

contradictions: Believes in institutional reform but has personally enabled an institutional cover-up
Projects absolute certainty but privately has not been certain of anything in three years
habits: Checks the time on her tactical eye every seventeen minutes exactly
Leaves a small data offering at the Stile shrine at the start of every shift
Counts exits in every room she enters
breaking_points: Someone hurting a child in her sight
Being directly ordered to falsify another report

timeline.event: Age 23 — Hired by Ferrogate Transit Security after two years on UBC
Age 28 — Promoted to Level 4 Officer, Kessler Interchange permanent post
Age 31 — Witnessed supervisor falsify use-of-force incident report; said nothing
Age 32 — Joined E.L.F. devotional circle focused on Stile, the Interchange spirit
Age 34 — Currently tracking the Tuesday freight anomaly
